### 1. Write a code to do "for loop" to increase the number of coefficients used in the training and 

#Apply the method to test data set, produce the same plot x-axis (Number of coefficients) and y-axis (accuracy score)

coeff_t = pca.transform(X_test)
accuracy_t = []
accuracy = []

for i in range(1,31):
    
    lr = sl.LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000000)
    lr.fit(coeff[:,:i],y_train)
    number_pred = lr.predict(coeff[:,:i])
    number_pred_t = lr.predict(coeff_t[:,:i])
    accuracy.append(sm.accuracy_score(y_train,number_pred))
    accuracy_t.append(sm.accuracy_score(y_test,number_pred_t))

print(accuracy)
### plot x-axis (Number of coefficients) and y-axis (accuracy score) 
plt.figure(figsize=(10,5))
plt.scatter(range(1,31),accuracy)
plt.xlabel('Number of coefficients')
plt.ylabel('Accuracy score')
plt.show()

7. Use Random forest and do the same analysis to obtain the accuracy score of the training dataset and the test data as a function of number of coefficients used in the training.¶

You need to also adjust the max_depth parameter and find the depth with best performance.¶

You can explore the parameters¶

(a) produce a plot with x-axis (max depth) and y-axis (number of coefficients) with colors indicating the accuracy score and¶

find the best accuracy score for each number of coefficients.¶

(b) Plot the number of coefficients vs best accuracy score for training and test dataset.¶

[15 points]¶

In [ ]:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
import numpy as np

### Finally, We use random forest to do the classification. 
### 7. Use Random forest and do the same analysis to obtain the accuracy score of 
# the training dataset and the test data as a function of number of coefficients used in the training. 


import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

max_depths = range(1, 11)
num_coefficients = range(1, 11)
accuracy_scores = np.zeros((len(max_depths), len(num_coefficients)))
accuracy_scores_test = np.zeros((len(max_depths), len(num_coefficients)))

for i, max_depth in enumerate(max_depths):
    for j, num_coeff in enumerate(num_coefficients):
        rf = RandomForestClassifier(max_depth=max_depth, random_state=42)
        rf.fit(coeff[:, :num_coeff], y_train)
        accuracy_scores[i, j] = sm.accuracy_score(y_train, rf.predict(coeff[:, :num_coeff]))
        
        accuracy_scores_test[i, j] = sm.accuracy_score(y_test, rf.predict(coeff_t[:, :num_coeff]))
    
    

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.imshow(accuracy_scores, interpolation='nearest', cmap='viridis', aspect='auto')
plt.colorbar()
plt.xticks(np.arange(len(max_depths)), max_depths)
plt.yticks(np.arange(len(num_coefficients)), num_coefficients)
plt.ylabel('Number of coefficients')
plt.xlabel('Max depth')
plt.title('Training Accuracy')

plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.imshow(accuracy_scores_test, interpolation='nearest', cmap='viridis', aspect='auto')
plt.colorbar()
plt.xticks(np.arange(len(max_depths)), max_depths)
plt.yticks(np.arange(len(num_coefficients)), num_coefficients)
plt.ylabel('Number of coefficients')
plt.xlabel('Max depth')
plt.title('Test Accuracy')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# (b) Plot the number of coefficients vs best accuracy score for training and test dataset
best_accuracy_train = np.max(accuracy_scores, axis=0)
best_accuracy_test = np.max(accuracy_scores_test, axis=0)


plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
plt.scatter(num_coefficients, best_accuracy_train, label='Training')
plt.scatter(num_coefficients, best_accuracy_test, label='Test')
plt.xlabel('Number of coefficients')
plt.ylabel('Best Accuracy score')
plt.legend()
plt.show()
